prior_findings.description: §27.S.6 push-away measurement surface absent — interventionRefused shape not emitted on WS bus
prior_findings.evidence: Commit 361c629a (deployed at /vessels/activity-api/src/routes/activities.ts, confirmed via grep count=2) adds async WS emission of type='intervention.refused' on every refusal path. Live probe confirmed: POST /v2/activities/recommend with expected_output_shapes=['shape_that_does_not_exist_xyz123'] returns HTTP 200 with refusal field populated (type='no_producer_for_expected_shapes'). The async bus emit fires in a void IIFE — failures are caught and logged but never block the HTTP response. ASSESSMENT: The measurement surface now exists and is live. However §27.S.6 requires measurement over 'sustained adversarial exposure' with substrate gates refusing operator interventions 'with cited evidence over a sustained window of adversarial exposure'. The current implementation: (1) emits the event, (2) returns refusal JSON to the caller, (3) does NOT yet record refusal events durably in SurrealDB for subsequent counting or attribution across sessions. No query surface for 'count interventions refused over last N hours' was found. The WS bus is ephemeral — events not delivered to a subscriber at emission time are lost. This is the minimum necessary surface to start accumulating the S3 signal, but sustained measurement requires a durable store or subscriber that counts. VERDICT: F-129 PARTIALLY_RESOLVED — emit surface exists and fires live; durable measurement for S3 assessment remains absent.
prior_findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight SurrealDB write (or durable counter) for each intervention.refused event so the refusal rate over time is queryable. Without this, §27.S.6 sustained-window assessment requires correlating ephemeral WS bus messages — unreliable.

new_findings.description: proposal non-executability — several proposal files use hallucinated resolver names not registered in the ias-executor-ts resolver registry
new_findings.detail: Audit of all 9 proposal files found resolver names that do not correspond to any registered resolver in development-vessel (31 registered resolvers listed in /shapes). HALLUCINATED resolvers found: activity_fetch (proposal-fm-17; used for raw SurrealQL via activity-api — no such resolver; would require surrealql or http_fetch), deterministic-projection, deterministic-classifier, impulse-emitter (proposal-fm-43; none of these exist in ias-executor-ts resolver registry), vessel_outbox_probe, vessel_registry_query, activity_api_query, deterministic_compose, deterministic_join, vessel_redelivery_dispatch (proposal-fm-44; none exist). REAL resolvers observed in proposals: llm_completion_dispatch, fs_write, surrealql (proposal-fm-43 uses surrealql — this IS a real resolver), bash (proposal-fp-15). The resolver_pattern_report aggregator confirms only real resolvers are appearing in actual trace data (16 unique resolvers seen over 24h). CONCLUSION: hallucinated resolvers are in draft proposal files only — they never ran and did not pollute the Thompson registry. However these proposals are permanently non-executable unless the hallucinated resolvers are either (a) implemented, or (b) replaced with equivalent real resolver calls.

resolver_check.note: activity_fetch IS registered in dev-vessel — but proposal-fm-17 uses it in a way that expects SQL query execution (raw SurrealQL), which is not how the activity_fetch resolver works (it fetches activity templates, not raw DB rows). This is a semantic mismatch even where the resolver name is correct.
resolver_check.json_path_extract_not_hallucinated: json_path_extract IS a real registered resolver in dev-vessel (src/resolvers/json-path-extract.ts). It appears in resolver_pattern_report with 8 executions, success_rate=0.750. NOT a hallucinated resolver.

new_findings.proposal_timestamp_issue: Proposals from subagent (proposal-fm-43-cascade-attribution-error, proposal-fp-11, proposal-fp-12, proposal-fp-15-missing-producer, proposal-fm-44-silent-trace-loss) could not be parsed as JSON due to embedded control characters — likely embedded newlines in the template JSON string field. This is a secondary defect. Readable proposals: proposal-fm-17 has created_at=1970-01-01T00:00:00.000Z (epoch), proposal-fm-43-attribution-cascade-witness-check has authored_at=2026-05-22T00:00:00Z, proposal-fm-44-trace-redelivery-monitor has created_at=2026-05-22T00:00:00Z (midnight, not actual timestamp). The epoch timestamp in proposal-fm-17 persists from prior audit finding and has NOT been corrected.
new_findings.recommendation: Before attempting to promote any proposal to the activity registry, validate all resolver names against the registered resolver list. For proposals using deterministic-projection/deterministic-classifier/impulse-emitter patterns, consider implementing these as thin wrappers in development-vessel or rewriting tasks using json_path_extract + llm_completion_dispatch + fs_write chains.

new_findings.description: resolver_pattern_report shape advertised but not accessible via CamelCase — query requires snake_case form
new_findings.detail: The development-vessel advertises 'resolver_pattern_report' (snake_case) in /shapes. The audit instructions referenced 'resolverPatternReport' (camelCase) which returns 'unknown shape'. This inconsistency with the dev-vessel's own shape naming convention (most other shapes are camelCase: memoryNote, coverageReport, etc.) creates a usability gap. The aggregator IS functional when queried with snake_case — it returned 20 rows / 16 unique resolvers across 24h window with total_observations=984.
new_findings.recommendation: Normalize resolver_pattern_report to resolverPatternReport in both the shape type definition and the dispatcher registration, matching the camelCase convention used by all other development-vessel shapes.

new_findings.description: S.4a criterion — temporal spread evidence exists across 4 cells (06:39–10:39 UTC) but coverage_fraction=0.593 with reachable_unlearned=18 out of 27 reachable shapes — sustained 4h spread present but learning is not converging toward completion
new_findings.detail: Coverage tick output: cells_over_time shows 4 non-overlapping hourly cells from 06:39 to 10:39 UTC 2026-05-27. All 4 cells have reachable_learned > 0 (3, 5, 7, 9 respectively — monotonically increasing). coverage_fraction=0.593, coverage_progress=True in the latest cell. S.4a requires 'at least one coverageReport impulse has coverage_progress=true from natural substrate activity' — this IS satisfied. However, 18 shapes remain unlearned in the latest cell. The rate of learning (2 new shapes/hour) projects full coverage at ~9 hours from now — well within the 4-hour window requirement. Boredom vessel is functioning (dispatched goals[0] and goals[1] since audit start). This finding is informational rather than blocking.
new_findings.recommendation: S.4a criterion as written (a single coverage_progress=true impulse from natural activity) appears to be met by the current coverage data. The operator should evaluate whether the checkbox in tasks.md can be marked complete, or whether a stronger interpretation (e.g., multiple consecutive cells) is intended. See F-128 for the related ambiguity.
